sentences.text: On a recent sunny day, 13,000 chickens roam over Larry Brown's 40 windswept acres in Shiner, Texas.
sentences.translation: 在最近一个阳光明媚的日子里,13000只鸡在德克萨斯州Shiner的Larry Brown那片40英亩的多风土地上漫步。一些鸡在停放的汽车阴影下休息。另一些则和奶牛一起喝水。这一切看似随意,但实际上是经过设计的,是这个价值61亿美元的美国鸡蛋产业押注的下一个大趋势的一部分:气候友好型鸡蛋。

sentences.text: Some rest in the shade of a parked car.
Others drink water with the cows.
This all seems random, but it's by design, part of what the $6.1 billion U.S. egg industry bets will be its next big thing: climate- friendly eggs.

These eggs, which are making their debut now on shelves for as much as $8 a dozen, are still labeled organic and animal-friendly, but they're also from birds that live on farms using regenerative agriculture—special techniques to cultivate rich soils that can trap greenhouse gases.
sentences.translation: 这些鸡蛋目前正在货架上首次亮相,售价高达每打8美元,它们仍然标有有机和动物友好的标签,但它们也来自生活在使用再生农业的农场上的鸟类——这种特殊技术培育能够捕获温室气体的肥沃土壤。这类鸡蛋可以作为帮助对抗气候变化的产品进行营销。

sentences.text: Such eggs could be marketed as helping to fight climate change.
The egg industry's push is the first major test of whether animal products from regenerative farms can become the next premium offering.
sentences.translation: 鸡蛋行业的推动是对来自再生农场的动物产品能否成为下一个高端产品的首次重大考验。在短短十多年里,有机鸡蛋从被视为天然食品商店的小众产品发展到在沃尔玛销售。最近,益生菌和植物基肉类也曾遭遇类似质疑,但两者都已爆发式增长成为超市的主要品类。如果可持续鸡蛋的推出取得成功,它可能为再生牛肉、西兰花及更多产品打开闸门。

sentences.text: In barely more than a decade, organic eggs went from being dismissed as a niche product in natural foods stores to being sold at Walmart.
More recently there were similar doubts about probiotics and plant-based meats, but both have exploded into major supermarket categories.
If the sustainable-egg rollout is successful, it could open the floodgates for regenerative beef, broccoli, and beyond.
The industry is betting that the same consumers paying more for premium attributes such as free-range, non-GMO, and pasture-raised eggs will embrace sustainability.
sentences.translation: 该行业押注那些愿意为自由放养、非转基因和牧场饲养等优质属性支付更多费用的消费者将会接受可持续性。调查显示,年轻一代更关注气候变化,植物基肉类的部分成功可以归因于购物者希望表明他们保护环境的愿望。Egg Innovations总裁John Brunnquell说,年轻人"真的很关心地球","他们正在彻底改变食物链,其影响甚至超出了我认为他们自己所理解的程度。"

sentences.text: Surveys show that younger generations are more concerned about climate change, and some of the success of plant-based meat can be chalked up to shoppers wanting to signal their desire to protect the environment.
Young adults "really care about the planet," says John Brunnquell, president of Egg Innovations.
"They are absolutely altering the food chain beyond what I think even they understand what they're doing."
More Americans are opting to work well into retirement, a growing trend that threatens to upend the old workforce model.
sentences.translation: 越来越多的美国人选择工作到退休后很久，这一日益增长的趋势可能会颠覆旧有的劳动力模式。

sentences.text: One in three Americans who are at least 40 have or plan to have a job in retirement to prepare for a longer life, according to a survey conducted by Harris Poll for TD Ameritrade.
sentences.translation: 根据Harris Poll为TD Ameritrade进行的一项调查，年龄至少40岁的美国人中有三分之一已经或计划在退休后找一份工作，为更长的寿命做准备。更令人惊讶的是，调查显示，超过半数的"不退休者"——那些计划在退休后工作或退休后重返工作岗位的人——表示即使有足够的钱安顿下来,他们也会在晚年继续工作。

sentences.text: Even more surprising is that more than half of "unretirees"—those who plan to work in retirement or went back to work after retiring—said they would be employed in their later years even if they had enough money to settle down, the survey showed.
Financial needs aren't the only culprit for the "unretirement" trend.
sentences.translation: 经济需求并非"不退休"趋势的唯一原因。根据该研究，其他原因包括个人成就感,如保持精神健康、防止无聊或避免抑郁。约72%的"不退休者"受访者表示,他们会在退休后重返工作以保持精神健康,而59%的人表示这与维持生计有关。懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2022-english-two/section2-part-a-2/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好

sentences.text: Other reasons, according to the study, include personal fulfillment such as staying mentally fit, preventing boredom or avoiding depression.
About 72% of "unretiree" respondents said that they would return to work once retired to keep mentally fit while 59% said it would be tied to making ends meet.
One reason for the change in retirement patterns: Americans are living longer.
sentences.translation: 退休模式改变的一个原因是:美国人的寿命更长了。根据美国人口普查局的数据,2018年65岁及以上人口占总人口的16%,比前一年增长32%。这也比2010年增长了30.2%。老年美国人也是美国劳动力中增长最快的群体,婴儿潮一代预计比前几代人更长寿。过去三十年中,退休年龄人口在劳动力中的比例翻了一番。根据资产管理公司United Income的数据,2月份约有20%的65岁及以上人口在劳动力队伍中,高于1985年1月10%的历史最低水平。

sentences.text: The share of the population 65 and older was 16% in 2018, up 32% from the prior year, according to the U.S. Census Bureau.
That's also up 30.2% since 2010.
Older Americans are also the fastest-growing segment of the US workforce, and boomers are expected to live longer than previous generations.
The percentage of retirement-age people in the labor force has doubled over the past three decades.
About 20% of people 65 and older were in the workforce in February, up from an all-time low of 10% in January 1985, according to money manager United Income.

Unfortunately, many people who are opting to work in retirement are preparing to do so because they are worried about making ends meet in their later years, said Brent Weiss, a co-founder at Baltimore-based financial-planning firm Facet Wealth.
sentences.translation: 位于Baltimore的财务规划公司Facet Wealth的联合创始人Brent Weiss表示,不幸的是,许多选择在退休后工作的人准备这样做是因为他们担心晚年无法维持生计。他建议即将退休的人应该与财务顾问交谈以设定长期财务目标。

sentences.text: He suggested that preretirees should speak with a financial adviser to set long-term financial goals.
We have all encountered them, in both our personal and professional lives.
sentences.translation: 我们在个人生活和职业生涯中都遇到过它们。想想那些让你感到被欺骗或沮丧的会员资格或订阅服务，它们注册过程无缝顺畅，但后来却很难取消。本应简单透明的事情却可能被有意或无意地复杂化，从而损害消费者的选择权。这些就是暗黑模式的例子。

sentences.text: Think about the times you felt tricked or frustrated by a membership or subscription that had a seamless sign-up process but was later difficult to cancel.
Something that should be simple and transparent can be complicated, intentionally or unintentionally, in ways that impair consumer choice.

Although ethics classes are common around the world, scientists are unsure if their lessons can actually change behavior; evidence either way is weak, relying on contrived laboratory tests or sometimes unreliable self-reports.
sentences.translation: 尽管伦理课程在世界各地很常见,但科学家们不确定这些课程是否真的能改变行为;无论哪种方向的证据都很薄弱,依赖于人为设计的实验室测试或有时不可靠的自我报告。但发表在《认知》期刊上的一项新研究发现,至少在一种真实世界的情况下,一堂伦理课可能产生了持久的影响。

sentences.text: But a new study published in Cognition found that, in at least one real-world situation, a single ethics lesson may have had lasting effects.

part_a.directions:
Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark
your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
Text 1
P1 On a recent sunny day, 13,000 chickens roam over Larry Brown's 40 windswept acres in Shiner,
Texas. Some rest in the shade of a parked car. Others drink water with the cows. This all seems random,
but it's by design, part of what the $6.1 billion U.S. egg industry bets will be its next big thing: climate-
friendly eggs.
在最近一个阳光明媚的日子里,13000只鸡在德克萨斯州Shiner的Larry Brown那片40英亩的多风土地上漫
步。一些鸡在停放的汽车阴影下休息。另一些则和奶牛一起喝水。这一切看似随意,但实际上是经过设计
的,是这个价值61亿美元的美国鸡蛋产业押注的下一个大趋势的一部分:气候友好型鸡蛋。
P2 These eggs, which are making their debut now on shelves for as much as $8 a dozen, are still
labeled organic and animal-friendly, but they're also from birds that live on farms using regenerative
agriculture—special techniques to cultivate rich soils that can trap greenhouse gases. Such eggs could be
marketed as helping to fight climate change.
这些鸡蛋目前正在货架上首次亮相,售价高达每打8美元,它们仍然标有有机和动物友好的标签,但它们也来
自生活在使用再生农业的农场上的鸟类——这种特殊技术培育能够捕获温室气体的肥沃土壤。这类鸡蛋可
以作为帮助对抗气候变化的产品进行营销。
P3 "I'm excited about our progress," says Brown, who harvests eggs for Denver-based Nest Fresh
Eggs and is adding more cover crops that draw worms and crickets for the chickens to eat. The birds'
waste then fertilizes fields. Such improvements "allow our hens to forage for higher-quality natural feed
that will be good for the land, the hens, and the eggs that we supply to our customers."
"我对我们的进展感到兴奋,"为位于丹佛的Nest Fresh Eggs收获鸡蛋的Brown说,他正在增加更多覆盖作物,
以吸引蚯蚓和蟋蟀供鸡食用。然后鸟类的粪便为田地施肥。这些改进"使我们的母鸡能够觅食更高质量的

天然饲料,这对土地、母鸡以及我们供应给客户的鸡蛋都有好处。"

farms can become the next premium offering. In barely more than a decade, organic eggs went from
being dismissed as a niche product in natural foods stores to being sold at Walmart. More recently there
were similar doubts about probiotics and plant-based meats, but both have exploded into major
supermarket categories. If the sustainable-egg rollout is successful, it could open the floodgates for
regenerative beef, broccoli, and beyond.
鸡蛋行业的推动是对来自再生农场的动物产品能否成为下一个高端产品的首次重大考验。在短短十多年里,
有机鸡蛋从被视为天然食品商店的小众产品发展到在沃尔玛销售。最近,益生菌和植物基肉类也曾遭遇类似
质疑,但两者都已爆发式增长成为超市的主要品类。如果可持续鸡蛋的推出取得成功,它可能为再生牛肉、
西兰花及更多产品打开闸门。
P5 Regenerative products could be a hard sell, because the concept is tough to define quickly, says
Julie Stanton, associate professor of agricultural economics at Pennsylvania State University Brandywine.
Such farming also brings minimal, if any, improvement to the food products (though some producers say
their eggs have more protein).
宾夕法尼亚州立大学Brandywine分校农业经济学副教授Julie Stanton说,再生产品可能难以销售,因为这个
概念很难快速定义。这种农业方式对食品本身的改善也极少,甚至没有(尽管一些生产商声称他们的鸡蛋含
有更多蛋白质)。
P6 The industry is betting that the same consumers paying more for premium attributes such as
free-range, non-GMO, and pasture-raised eggs will embrace sustainability. Surveys show that younger
generations are more concerned about climate change, and some of the success of plant-based meat can
be chalked up to shoppers wanting to signal their desire to protect the environment. Young adults "really
care about the planet," says John Brunnquell, president of Egg Innovations. "They are absolutely altering
the food chain beyond what I think even they understand what they're doing."

性。调查显示,年轻一代更关注气候变化,植物基肉类的部分成功可以归因于购物者希望表明他们保护环境
的愿望。Egg Innovations总裁John Brunnquell说,年轻人"真的很关心地球","他们正在彻底改变食物链,
其影响甚至超出了我认为他们自己所理解的程度。"

[ A ]reducing the damage of worms.
[ B ]accelerating the disposal of waste.
[ C ]creating a sustainable system.
[ D ]attracting customers to his products.

P1 More Americans are opting to work well into retirement, a growing trend that threatens to upend
the old workforce model.

[ B ]boredom can be relieved after retirement.

Directions:
Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark
your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
Text 3
P1 We have all encountered them, in both our personal and professional lives. Think about the
times you felt tricked or frustrated by a membership or subscription that had a seamless sign-up process
but was later difficult to cancel. Something that should be simple and transparent can be complicated,
intentionally or unintentionally, in ways that impair consumer choice. These are examples of dark
patterns.
我们在个人生活和职业生涯中都遇到过它们。想想那些让你感到被欺骗或沮丧的会员资格或订阅服务，它
们注册过程无缝顺畅，但后来却很难取消。本应简单透明的事情却可能被有意或无意地复杂化，从而损害
消费者的选择权。这些就是暗黑模式的例子。
P2 First coined in 2010 by user experience expert Harry Brignull, "dark patterns" is a catch-all term
for practices that manipulate user interfaces to influence the decision-making ability of users. Brignull
identifies 12 types of common dark patterns, ranging from misdirection and hidden costs to "roach
motel", where a user experience seems easy and intuitive at the start, but turns difficult when the user
tries to get out.
2010年由用户体验专家Harry Brignull首次提出，"暗黑模式"是一个概括性术语，指操纵用户界面以影响
用户决策能力的做法。Brignull识别出12种常见的暗黑模式类型，从误导和隐藏成本到"蟑螂旅馆"，即用
户体验在开始时看起来简单直观，但当用户试图退出时却变得困难。
P3 In a 2019 study of 53,000 product pages and 11,000 websites, researchers found that about one
in 10 employs these design practices. Though widely prevalent, the concept of dark patterns is still not

well understood. Business and nonprofit leaders should be aware of dark patterns and try to avoid the
gray areas they engender.
在2019年一项对53000个产品页面和11000个网站的研究中，研究人员发现约十分之一采用了这些设计做
法。尽管广泛流行，暗黑模式的概念仍未被充分理解。企业和非营利组织领导者应该意识到暗黑模式，并
努力避免它们所产生的灰色地带。
P4 Where is the line between ethical, persuasive design and dark patterns? Businesses should
engage in conversations with IT, compliance, risk, and legal teams to review their privacy policy, and
include in the discussion the customer/user experience designers and coders responsible for the company's
user interface, as well as the marketers and advertisers responsible for sign-ups, checkout baskets,
pricing, and promotions. Any or all these teams can play a role in creating or avoiding "digital
deception."
道德的、具有说服力的设计与暗黑模式之间的界限在哪里?企业应该与IT、合规、风险和法律团队展开对
话，审查其隐私政策，并将负责公司用户界面的客户/用户体验设计师和编码人员，以及负责注册、结账
篮、定价和促销的营销人员和广告商纳入讨论。这些团队中的任何一个或全部都可能在创造或避免"数字
欺骗"中发挥作用。
P5 Lawmakers and regulators are slowly starting to address the ambiguity around dark patterns,
most recently at the state level. In March, the California Attorney General announced the approval of
additional regulations under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) that "ensure that consumers
will not be confused or misled when seeking to exercise their data privacy rights. The regulations aim to
ban dark patterns—this means prohibiting companies from using confusing language or unnecessary steps
such as forcing them to click through multiple screens or listen to reasons why they shouldn't opt out."
立法者和监管机构正在缓慢开始解决暗黑模式周围的模糊性问题，最近主要在州一级。3月，加州总检察
长宣布批准California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA)下的附加法规，"确保消费者在寻求行使其数据隐私
权时不会感到困惑或被误导。这些法规旨在禁止暗黑模式——这意味着禁止公司使用令人困惑的语言或不
必要的步骤，例如强迫他们点击多个屏幕或听取他们不应该选择退出的理由。"
P6 As more states consider promulgating additional regulations, there is a need for greater
accountability from within the business community. Dark patterns also can be addressed on a self-
regulatory basis, but only if organizations hold themselves accountable, not just to legal requirements but
also to industry best practices and standards.
随着更多州考虑颁布额外的法规，商业界需要更大的问责制。暗黑模式也可以在自律的基础上得到解决，
但前提是组织不仅要对法律要求负责，还要对行业最佳实践和标准负责。

realise that when one door closes, another opens. You also quickly learn to adapt and come up with

come to life the way that you expected.

second nature.

英语二真题(2022)
Section IV Part A
Directions:
Suppose you are planning a campus food festival. Write an e-mail to the international students in your
university to
1) introduce the food festival, and
2) invite them to participate.
You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET.
Do not use your own name. Use “Li Ming" instead. (10 points)
part_a.sample:
写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
Dear international students,
I am Li Ming, chairman of the Student Union. I am writing to warmly invite you to our campus food festival.
The festival will be held on the school playground from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. next Saturday. During the event, you
can taste a wide variety of delicious dishes from different regions of China and enjoy exciting cooking shows.
We sincerely hope you can join us. It is a wonderful chance to experience Chinese food culture and make new
friends. Please come and share the joy with us! Looking forward to your participation.
Yours, Li Ming
